summary: Verified the Madhuri→Nidhi session-mixing hotfix. Backend: 6/6 pytest cases pass (test_session_mixing_hotfix.py) confirming distinct refresh tokens per user, single-use rotation, and identity-owner integrity of /api/auth/refresh — user A's refresh never leaks user B's identity. Frontend: Playwright reproduced the exact reported scenario — logged in as User A (hr6@vhc.in Diya), simulated 'closed browser without logout' by removing only vhc_token + vhc_user while keeping A's vhc_refresh_token, then logged in as User B (hr12@vhc.in Sachin) on the same browser. Verified: (1) A's stale vhc_refresh_token was purged BEFORE B's session was written (new token differs from A's), (2) vhc_user is B, (3) using the current stored refresh_token against /api/auth/refresh returns hr12@vhc.in (never hr6). Sidebar UI also correctly reflects Sachin/hr12@vhc.in after the second login. Regression re-login (B→A) also rotates the refresh_token cleanly.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.js login() correctly purges vhc_token/vhc_refresh_token/vhc_user/vhc_requires_reset BEFORE writing new session values, and uses removeItem() (not setItem(k, null)) when server response lacks refresh_token — fix is correct.

Defensive suggestion (non-blocking): the AuthProvider useEffect on mount could also verify localStorage vhc_user.id === /auth/me response id (if getMe returns a different id, force logout). This would add a second line of defense against any future regression that re-introduces token cross-contamination.
seed_data_creation: No new users created — used existing hr6@vhc.in (Diya) and hr12@vhc.in (Sachin) from /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The frontend hotfix in /app/frontend/src/lib/auth.js login() is verified. Backend refresh endpoint behavior is unchanged (correctly returns owner identity per refresh_token). If regressing, use test_session_mixing_hotfix.py plus the Playwright scenario: login A → clear vhc_token+vhc_user (keep vhc_refresh_token) → login B → assert localStorage.vhc_refresh_token != A's original and that POST /api/auth/refresh with the stored token returns B.
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: previous login flow overwrote vhc_token but NOT vhc_refresh_token when a stale value from a prior user was still present in localStorage (typical scenario: previous user closed browser without clicking Logout). The axios 401 interceptor read the surviving stale refresh_token and hit /api/auth/refresh, which correctly issued an access token for the STALE token's owner — flipping the current session to the old user. Fix: auth.js login() now unconditionally removes vhc_token, vhc_refresh_token, vhc_user, and vhc_requires_reset BEFORE writing the new session's values, and explicitly removes vhc_refresh_token if the server response has no refresh_token (never leaves a stale value).
